angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,295,806 km at 26.73 pc = 3.65 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 27628: distance 26.731 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 26.731 +/- 0.08 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 36.9038 +/- 0.1345 mas (same row, RUWE 2.32), 274.4 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 10.487 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 27628: radius 10.487 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 46.438 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.054) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 7,295,806 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4656 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 27628: effective temperature 4656 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.069) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 27628: effective temperature 4656 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.069) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Burnashev (1985), Abastumani Astrophys. Obs. Bull. 59, 83; VizieR III/126, part2 record 75 (BS 2040), cross-checked against Gaia DR3 XP spectrum, source 2887731882922767744 (78 levels apart at most, the threshold is 12)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.59 from 2024A&A...683A.125P; the 8 published values span log g 2.48 to 2.8, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...683A.125P)
